correctness.rationale: Proved bounded host/parasite subsystem with host exponentially tending zero and parasite to k3; bounded asymptotically autonomous scalar commensal dynamics converge to 0, u-, or u+. Ordered scalar flow and hyperbolic sink basins force a single separating initial value, uniqueness follows from positive limiting difference exponent lambda-. The stable-manifold pullback at the hyperbolic intermediate equilibrium yields exact bounded first variation and positive finite integral. Logistic flow is strictly ordered in z0. The checker validates only algebraic special cases; no finite test substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: Two positive equilibrium roots themselves predate the source (2021 JTAM) and are excluded from novelty. The finding instead proves an all-initial-data three-way global basin law plus a first-order quantitative host/parasite-sensitive threshold not stated in the inspected same-equation full-text papers. General scalar ordering does not by itself deliver the global stability partition, strict threshold shift and explicit sensitivity without the displayed estimates.
residual_risks: Search coverage cannot prove global uniqueness; unindexed papers on exact basin geometry for this specific three-species harvest law may exist.

The 2026 related two-dimensional Allee paper was accessible through abstract, not enough for a whole-document noncoverage conclusion, but has a different model and does not create a decisive unresolved implication.

value.rationale: This open, structurally motivated bistable harvesting region has two competing attractors so local equilibria alone cannot decide extinction versus persistence for actual initial populations. The exact global basin threshold and first-order host rescue coefficient with strict initial parasite monotonicity resolve this natural decision problem, rather than selecting an arbitrary slice or repackaging known roots.
